chunks: What was narrated by Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, who said:

I said to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام: Our companions differ regarding the supererogatory salat; some of them pray forty-four, and some of them pray fifty. So inform me of that which you yourself practice, how it is, so that I may act likewise.

He said: “I pray fifty-one rakʿahs.” Then he said: “Count,” and he folded with his hand: “At zawāl, eight; four after ẓuhr; four before ʿaṣr; two rakʿahs after maghrib; two rakʿahs before the later ʿishāʾ; and two rakʿahs after ʿishāʾ while sitting, which are counted as one rakʿah while standing; and eight for salat al-layl; and al-witr, three; and the two rakʿahs of fajr; and the obligatory prayers, seventeen. That is fifty-one rakʿahs.”
And this also indicates that the sunnah (recommended practice) is what we have mentioned.

key_terms.صَلَاةَ ٱللَّيْلِ: the night prayer performed as a recommended act of worship
key_terms.صَلَاةِ ٱلتَّطَوُّعِ: supererogatory salat; the non-obligatory recommended prayers
key_terms.وَاحِدَةً وَخَمْسِينَ رَكْعَةً: fifty-one rakʿahs; the full total of obligatory and recommended daily prayers
key_terms.ٱلزَّوَالَ: the time after the sun passes its zenith, when the noon nawāfil are performed
key_terms.ٱلْمَسْنُونَ: that which is established as sunnah, meaning the recommended prescribed practice
key_terms.ٱلْوَتْرَ: the concluding unit(s) of the night prayer mentioned here as three rakʿahs

ai.seo_question: How many daily rakʿahs are included in the obligatory and recommended salat according to the hadith of Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states the total daily number of rakʿahs in the obligatory and recommended salat as fifty-one, according to the practice described by Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام. It details the distribution of the nawāfil around the daily prayers, including the night prayer, and serves as a jurisprudential basis for the prescribed recommended salat.
